epic.title: compat(update): autoUpdater and electron-updater facades over the host-owned KEL-53 updater, keld.build.ts translation, bridge release recipe
epic.body:
## Scope
`autoUpdater` (10 members, macOS+Windows) plus the ecosystem reality: draw.io uses electron-updater v6 (setFeedURL provider github, autoDownload=false, downloadUpdate, download-progress, quitAndInstall) with five electron-builder configs and @electron/fuses; Zettlr ships its own downloader. Live today: keld-update verifies signed v0 manifests/full packages, Windows extraction/staging/journaled activation and startup repair; keld-pack streams Windows v0 packages; `keld build`/`migrate` reserved; no update channel to Bun; no keld.build.ts schema.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: both facades exist; feed-URL writes are recorded no-ops ▲; `checkForUpdates` emits a typed error only when invoked without a host updater.
- L1: KEL-53 state machine events reach Bun (checking/available/not-available/progress/downloaded/error) with versions/dates/sizes, never paths.
- L2: `quitAndInstall` ordering split by facade × platform passes pinned entries; bridge release recipe validated on Windows NSIS (publisher match) and macOS.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-53 (host-owned updater: full-package activation first), KEL-254/KEL-270 (Windows install modes/journal), KEL-19/KEL-15 (keld.build.ts schema — RFC text missing), KEL-103/KEL-141/KEL-137 (macOS package cells), KEL-98 (contract source for update.* calls).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- Two thin Bun facades over one host state machine; electron-updater rewritten by migrate to a Keld shim exporting the AppUpdater subset draw.io exercises; pin 6.8.9.
- `setFeedURL` is accepted and recorded (never thrown — draw.io routes throws to a user-facing Update Error dialog); mismatch vs `keld.build.ts` feed → dev diagnostic; the host never reads it; `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` written into the host-declared role environment by migrate; never a fabricated `update-not-available`.
- `update-downloaded` = staged-and-verified (not published); `quitAndInstall` → host activation with health check and rollback; ordering atoms split per facade × platform (macOS native inverts before-quit).
- Authority: all network/verify/stage/activate/relaunch in the host; Bun gets `update.check/download/quitAndInstall` guarded calls (new guard operations need KEL-102 admission; contract source is open).
- Bridge release: Windows NSIS requires the Keld installer be signed by the same publisher (publisherName verification is skipped when absent from app-update.yml); macOS zip/latest-mac.yml path; Linux AppImage/deb per electron-updater ≥ 6.x sentinel.

decision_tickets.title: Who owns the compiled-in feed base (KEL-53/KEL-19 amendment) that autoUpdater.getFeedURL reports and setFeedURL is compared against?
decision_tickets.question: The host feed identity is compiled into the signed host (ExpectedAppIdentity) but no owner names the feed base field; `keld.build.ts` has no schema. Name the owner and the field before any facade contract; record the ▲ per platform (Windows: one `error` event "Update URL is not set"; macOS: no event — inference needing one Electron run).

edge_problems.problem: Missing gates: the proof ticket is blocked only by X02-T3 and X01-T2. It consumes none of the implementation it scores and neither PANEL-P1 (sync dialog outcome) nor PANEL-P3 (denominator draft). X01-T2 (lifecycle-family recorder) is not a real gate — product cells reuse the KEL-237 runner pattern, not the recorder.

Missing gates: it emits keld.build.ts 'per F09-T2' (schema does not exist; F09-A6 open), enumerated `el:` channels into windows.<w>.channels (parse-and-ignore until F04-A1), and — per PANEL-D14 — DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE into a host-declared role environment that is not in its five-file list.
edge_problems.fix: Edges X02-T3 ← F04-A1 and ← F09-A6 (or drop keld.build.ts from the first-proof artifact); add the role-environment output and its owning schema to the ticket.

edge_problems.problem: F09-A2 (compiled-in feed base owner) gates the whole ticket, but the first-proof slice (inert electron-updater adapter with recorded setFeedURL) reads no feed.
edge_problems.fix: Split the adapter slice out with no F09-A2 edge.

invariant_violations.violation: 'Compat lands a conformance entry (citing the pinned Electron doc sentence) before implementation' — F07, F08, F09 and X03 have no conformance ticket and these implementation tickets have no conformance-entry predecessor.
invariant_violations.fix: Add a conformance entry ticket (or an explicit first AC 'entry lands first, cites sentence') per family; for first proof at least F07 (preload order, sandboxed require error text) and F09 (setFeedURL never throws).

quality_problems.problem: Oversized: F06-T2 (4 dialog kinds × sync variants + scope minting + parenting, two review gates), F06-T4 (Menu + Tray), F06-T5 (4 modules, 27 members), F06-T6 (11 modules), F01-T5 (lock + second-instance + open-file + open-url + protocol client), F09-T1 (KEL-53 state machine + guarded calls + two facades).
quality_problems.fix: Split along the first-proof slices named in the yagni rows; each slice one concern, one review gate set.

yagni.reason: Slice only: an inert electron-updater adapter — autoUpdater.logger.transports.*, autoDownload, autoInstallOnAppQuit are set unconditionally at import (:82-86), on('error') is registered at top level (:2233) and setFeedURL runs outside the disable guard (:2078). Park the KEL-53 state machine, update.* guarded calls and quitAndInstall.

The proof runs under `keld dev`; nothing reads keld.build.ts, its schema does not exist (KEL-15 body is only the RFC brief — Linear, fetched 2026-10-06), and the bridge-release recipe is distribution polish that #312 orders after the migration proof.

hidden_coupling.coupling: Updater disablement depends on an environment variable: PANEL-D14 has migrate write DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true into 'the host-declared role environment', read at module top level (:75). That is a boot fact delivered at spawn (F01-T4 / KEL-75 no-inherited-env) and a migrate output not present in X02-T3's file list. If it is absent, the boot-time checkForUpdates runs (:2092-2100) and F09-T1's 'typed error on explicit check' fires at activation.
hidden_coupling.fix: Name the declared-role-environment field and its schema owner; add it to X02-T3 outputs and to F01-T4's payload; F09-T1 AC covers both env-present and env-absent boots.

hidden_coupling.coupling: X02-T3's byte-identical artefact includes keld.build.ts 'per F09-T2', whose schema has no text anywhere (KEL-15 body is only a brief). Changing the build schema later silently invalidates the golden artefact that defines the generator.
hidden_coupling.fix: Remove keld.build.ts from the first-proof artefact (nothing reads it under keld dev) or add the edge and accept the delay.

hidden_coupling.coupling: Every 'Current behavior' line was verified by refuters at origin/main d150a14; main is now b4b907c3 (5 commits: KEL-270 S5/S8 runtime/guard, KEL-19 T1 ExpectedAppIdentity container, KEL-254). F09-A2 (feed base in ExpectedAppIdentity) and the role-spawn facts in F01-T4/X03-T1 touch code that moved.
hidden_coupling.fix: Stamp each ticket with the verification SHA; re-verify F09-A2, F01-T4, X03-T1 at b4b907c3 before they are taken.

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse (four uniques; default-deny; no Electron-isms in core/ipc; no parallel owners; reuse KEL-53/74/75/79/80/98/102/135/254; measured perf; spec+Linear gate; #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127 direction)

verdicts.reason: Corpus facts check out (draw.io src/main/electron.js:17-18 imports electron-updater, :85-86 autoDownload=false/autoInstallOnAppQuit=silentUpdate, :2078 setFeedURL github provider, :2099 checkForUpdates, :2350 quitAndInstall; Zettlr uses got+sha256+shell.openPath). Arch 04 §4 Tier 2 lists 'autoUpdater→keld-update adapter', §2 says migrate replaces 'electron*' deps with '@keld/*' deps (so a Keld-owned electron-updater-shaped package is within the five-file contract), and §7's bridge presupposes electron-updater clients. One host state machine with thin facades respects one-owner and the four uniques. Two accounting claims are wrong and must be corrected (see correction).
verdicts.evidence: docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md lines 36-45, 138-141, 194-200; docs/specs/kel74-compat-evidence-schema.md lines 149, 159-167 (`kind` closed set install|activation|primary_workflow|full_feature; 'Electron API scoreboard rows stay narrative until a committed product denominator'); scratchpad corpus drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js lines 17-18, 84-86, 2078-2082, 2350; Linear KEL-17 status Done (RFC) with no docs/specs entry.
verdicts.correction: (1) KEL-74 has no 'L3 ecosystem row' concept: `kind` is a closed set and Electron API rows are narrative. Record the shim as cells inside the draw.io product denominator (e.g. primary_workflow/full_feature cells for 'check → download → quitAndInstall') plus narrative scoreboard rows; do not invent a new denominator kind without a KEL-74 schema bump. (2) Order by demand (root AGENTS YAGNI): the electron-updater-shaped shim has corpus demand (draw.io); the 10-member Electron-core autoUpdater facade has zero corpus demand across all three apps and should be the second slice, kept only because arch 04 §4 Tier 2 names it. (3) KEL-17 is Done in Linear but its migrate/shim UX is not in the repo; the shim needs its own spec+issue (GitHub, Linear at cap).

verdicts.reason: The policy (host-owned feed, app-selected URL never honored, allowDowngrade/allowAnyVersion impossible under the monotonic floor) survives and is well sourced. The stated mechanism does not: the object says the feed URL is 'compiled into the signed host (ExpectedAppIdentity)' and that getFeedURL 'returns the host's compiled-in feed base from ExpectedAppIdentity'. ExpectedAppIdentityPayload carries only app_id, channel, target and update_public_key; arch 06 §4a step 1 says the host carries 'the key, app id, channel and target'; KEL-254 provenance v2 lists app id, channel, target, mode, owner, roots, baseline, key identity, channel owner — no feed base. No Keld source names an owner for `<feed-base>`.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-pack/src/expected_identity.rs lines 52-60 (struct fields: app_id, channel, target, update_public_key); docs/architecture/06-runtime-and-tooling.md lines 633-636 (`<feed-base>` placeholder) and 869-875 (compiled-in = key, app id, channel, target); grep of docs/specs/kel53-full-package-activation.md and kel254-*.md for 'feed-base|feed base|feed URL' returns no owner; docs/specs/kel53 §'Trust, package and channel ownership' lists no feed origin.
verdicts.correction: Name the feed-base owner before any facade contract: the cheapest consistent choice is a KEL-53/KEL-19 amendment adding the feed base (or a feed-origin identity) to the signed host identity or to installer provenance v2 — one owner, byte-validated like the other fields — with keld.build.ts `update.feed` as its build-time input. Until that lands, getFeedURL has no source of truth and the conformance entry must be 'unknown', not ▲. Keep setFeedURL as accepted-and-ignored with a dev diagnostic only after a code is allocated (KELD-COMPAT-001..009 are keld-compat evidence-parser codes, and the registry rejects un-emitted codes).

verdicts.reason: State mapping matches landed code and spec: completed stage 'is neither published nor selected' (product-status row 9; arch 06 §4), activation runs journaled publish → candidate launch → 30 s Ready health → commit/rollback with floor unchanged on rollback (KEL-53 criteria 8-9), errors are typed KELD-UPDATE-001..018 and 'CLI/compat render them without remapping' (KEL-53 line 1830), Channel enum is Stable/Beta/Canary, manifest has publishedAt and no release notes. Electron docs confirm quitAndInstall/before-quit-for-update semantics. Two of the author's unknowns are now settled by sources (see correction).
verdicts.evidence: docs/specs/kel53-full-package-activation.md lines 512-531 (criterion 8: candidate 'must have booted from that exact version, reached application Ready, and remained alive for 30 monotonic seconds'; criterion 9 rollback), 1473 ('starts the app and reports boot, Ready and health'), 1830; docs/engineering/product-status.tsv row 9; docs/architecture/06 lines 644-660 (publishedAt, no releaseNotes); crates/keld-update/src/error.rs lines 300-317, 445-451; crates/keld-update/src/lib.rs lines 84-95; electron-builder v26.0.12 AppUpdater.ts (checkForUpdates emits 'error' AND rethrows); Electron v44.4.5 auto-updater.md quitAndInstall/before-quit-for-update.
verdicts.correction: (1) Unknown 'quit without relaunch' is answered by KEL-53: there is no headless health boot — the candidate 'starts the app' and must reach Ready; so electron-updater's silent install-at-quit without relaunch (autoInstallOnAppQuit / isForceRunAfter=false) cannot be honored. Record a ▲: Keld either relaunches the app as the candidate at quit, or defers activation to the next user launch (which then pays publish+candidate boot+30 s health). This must be a recorded divergence, not an owner choice. (2) Unknown 'does electron-updater reject and emit' is settled at v26.0.12: checkForUpdates emits 'error' and rethrows; the shim's exactly-once emission + rejected promise is therefore itself a ▲ versus electron-updater (draw.io's 5 s dedupe tolerates it) and must be entered as such.

verdicts.reason: Authority placement (all network/verify/stage/activate in the host; roles get no paths; no installer spawn) is correct and matches KEL-53 non-goals and arch 03 broker pattern. Three mechanism claims fail: (a) 'generated through the existing KEL-98 echo-codegen contract source' — KEL-98 is explicitly 'a bootstrap for the existing echo vertical slice, not Keld's general contract', non-goal 'no general ... IDL, or arbitrary schema generator', and product-status says general schema codegen is absent; today @keld/api channels.ts hard-codes a single echoChannel and rejects any other descriptor. (b) 'Grants are declared in keld.permissions.jsonc' — KEL-53 §'Capabilities, wire and errors' states 'Application permissions cannot grant update authority. No KIPC, renderer bridge or permission-manifest change is introduced', and keld-guard today evaluates only dotted fs.* capabilities with path scopes; an update.* grant is a guard/KEL-102 schema change needing its own spec. (c) The object names the install grant `update.quitAndInstall` in A4 and `update.install` in security_mapping — two names for one rule.
verdicts.evidence: docs/specs/kel98-echo-codegen.md lines 19-25, 93-94, 219; docs/engineering/product-status.tsv row 23 ('general schema codegen ... remain absent'); packages/@keld/api/src/channels.ts lines 55-66 ('channel descriptor is not declared by this Keld build'); docs/specs/kel53-full-package-activation.md lines 1819-1822; crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs lines 6, 672, 730, 1016 (fs.read|fs.write only); packages/@keld/api/src/link.ts lines 176-183 (host→Bun Event frames exist: ready / last-window-closed); docs/architecture/02-ipc.md lines 248-256, 389 (credit windows 'remain later work').
verdicts.correction: (1) State the dependency honestly: update.check/download/install need either the absent general contract source (`@keld/schema`/`keld gen`, KEL-98 owner's successor) or a hand-written typed lifecycle-channel extension like the KEL-142 slice; the F09 ticket must consume that owner, not claim KEL-98 echo-codegen covers it. (2) Reconcile with KEL-53 via an amendment that distinguishes 'trigger a host-owned, host-verified check/activation' (a grantable app capability) from 'update authority' (never grantable); extend keld-guard's capability schema under KEL-102 rather than special-casing. (3) Resolve the unknown: unsolicited host→Bun events exist (Event frames on the lifecycle channel) but credit-window backpressure is not live, so progress must be latest-value-wins coalesced on the host. (4) One grant name (`update.install`) everywhere.

verdicts.reason: The client-side constraints are confirmed at electron-updater v26.0.12: NsisUpdater.doInstall args are exactly --updated, /S (silent), --force-run, /D=<installDirectory>, --package-file; verifySignature fails with 'New version X is not signed by the application owner' (ERR_UPDATER_INVALID_SIGNATURE); elevate.exe when isAdminRightsRequired, EACCES→elevate, ENOENT→shell.openPath. draw.io electron-builder-win.json confirms nsis.perMachine=true and publisherName ['JGraph Ltd','draw.io Ltd']. Keld constraints confirmed: KEL-53 first cell is windows-x64 only, MachineUacDirect (T4d) unimplemented, KEL-137 In Progress and a predecessor for every macOS/Linux cell, KEL-103 still draft (kel139 line 432), arch 06 §4a feed is static files. Ordering Windows x64 first follows.
verdicts.evidence: electron-builder v26.0.12 NsisUpdater.ts (fetched 2026-10-06); scratchpad corpus drawio-desktop/electron-builder-win.json (perMachine true, publisherName list, nsis+msi targets); docs/specs/kel53-full-package-activation.md lines 185-215, 226-229, 388-392; docs/specs/kel139-macos-product-spine.md line 432; Linear KEL-137 status In Progress; docs/architecture/06 lines 427-441, 492, 629-636; product-status row 10 (installers/signing absent).
verdicts.correction: Add two receipts the object lacks: (1) publisherName verification is read from app-update.yml on disk and is SKIPPED when absent — so the Authenticode-publisher constraint binds draw.io (configured) but is not a universal bridge requirement; (2) for draw.io specifically the Windows bridge is blocked twice, not once: Keld's installer must honor /D=<Program Files dir> + /S under electron-updater's elevate.exe flow, and that is a machine install → MachineUacDirect (T4d) must land first or the bridge must be an explicit owner decision to leave a stale per-machine Electron install. Mark the bridge 'blocked on T4d' for draw.io rather than 'reachable for Windows x64'.

verdicts.reason: The disposition table is consistent with sources (arch 04 §2 keld.build.ts row; arch 06 §3 signers rcodesign/signtool/osslsigncode; fuse defaults per research 186; KEL-75 no inherited env/argv; keld-pack ExpectedAppIdentity app id; corpus configs verified). But the decision cannot be settled: keld.build.ts has no schema anywhere in the repo, and KEL-15 ('RFC: Configuration schema') is marked Done in Linear (2026-07-10) with no docs/specs artifact — so the target the translation generates into is unowned in-repo. The proposal also asserts a 'sandboxed Bun subprocess' for forge.config.js evaluation; no such tooling sandbox exists (KEL-78 strict profile is for app roles) and arch 03 says migrate seeds via static analysis.
verdicts.evidence: grep for 'keld.build' across docs/crates/packages: only docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md lines 27, 38 and 06 line 440; Linear KEL-15 status Done, no docs/specs/kel15-*; docs/architecture/03-security.md lines 213-216 ('keld migrate seeds the manifest from static analysis'); docs/specs/kel75-principalized-bun-child-roles.md lines 142, 367; docs/research/library/compatibility-competitors/186-electron-micro-surfaces.md fuse sub-ledger; scratchpad corpus drawio-desktop/electron-builder-win.json, zettlr/forge.config.js lines 4-46, zettlr/electron-builder.yml lines 49-94.
verdicts.correction: Missing evidence: the KEL-15 RFC text (Linear says Done; repo has nothing). Cheapest step: ask the KEL-15 owner (GYLDLAB) for the accepted RFC and land it as docs/specs/kel15-config-schema.md, or open a successor issue that owns keld.build.ts's schema (identity, targets, installMode, signing, update.feed/channel) before migrate translation is specified. Replace 'sandboxed Bun subprocess' with an honest policy: static parse of JSON/YAML; for executable forge configs require `--config-json` or an explicit `--eval-config` run as the developer with a warning (no sandbox claim).

extra_findings.finding: Spec/spec tension the object missed: architecture 03 §3 says `keld migrate` seeds the permission manifest with 'autoUpdater → net to feed URL' (an app-role network grant toward the feed), while KEL-53 says 'Application permissions cannot grant update authority' and arch 06 §4a makes the host the only feed client. One of the two must change; the F09 ticket should name this as a doc fix (code/spec mismatch rule) and not cite arch 03 line 215 as support for a host-owned grant.

extra_findings.finding: Feed-base ownership gap: no Keld artifact (ExpectedAppIdentity, provenance v2, KEL-53 spec, arch 06) names where `<feed-base>` comes from or how it is bound to the signed host. Every facade claim about getFeedURL, setFeedURL cross-checks and the bridge feed layout depends on this unowned field.

New codes must be allocated in docs/engineering/keld-error-codes.md with emitting code ('the registry rejects un-emitted codes'), or the facade diagnostics need their own family.

extra_findings.finding: The object's `update.*` events assume a backpressured host→Bun stream (KEL-80). Today unsolicited Event frames exist only on the lifecycle channel with two decoded events (ready, last-window-closed) and credit windows are 'later work'; a progress stream must be host-coalesced (latest value wins) and declared on the lifecycle/app-link receive policy, otherwise a flood of download-progress frames violates invariant 7 (no unbounded queues).

extra_findings.finding: Prior-decision alignment: KEL-15 and KEL-17 are both 'Done' RFCs in Linear with no repo spec, and `keld migrate`/`keld build` are KELD-CLI-045 reserved. Under the spec+Linear gate (invariant 6) every F09 implementation slice (facade, shim, migrate translation, bridge recipe) needs a new approved spec and GitHub issue; the object does not say which existing Linear owner each slice consumes versus which needs a new ticket.

research.summary: Electron's autoUpdater is a 10-member module (setFeedURL/getFeedURL/checkForUpdates/quitAndInstall + 6 events), macOS+Windows only, that delegates verification and installation to Squirrel.Mac / Squirrel.Windows / MSIX and takes an app-selected feed URL [fact: v44.4.5 auto-updater.md]. Neither corpus app uses it directly: draw.io uses electron-updater v6 (setFeedURL({provider:'github',...}), autoDownload=false, autoInstallOnAppQuit, downloadUpdate, download-progress, info.version, logger) and Zettlr ships its own got-based downloader (shell.openPath of the downloaded installer + app.quit) [fact: corpus grep]. Keld today: keld-update implements signed v0 manifest/full verification, Windows x64 extraction/staging, PerUserDirect journaled activation, read-only active selection and startup repair; keld-pack streams Windows v0 packages only; keld-cli `build`/`migrate` are reserved (KELD-CLI-045); @keld/electron exports only `app`; no update event channel to Bun, no keld.build.ts schema, no autoUpdater facade, no bridge recipe [fact: product-status.tsv rows 9/10/13, crates, packages]. Feed orchestration, candidate launch, 30-second health, host consumer, macOS/Linux package cells (blocked on KEL-137 + KEL-103) are TARGET. Design answer: implement ONE host-owned updater (KEL-53) and expose two thin Bun facades over kipc — Electron-core `autoUpdater` and an electron-updater-shaped shim for migrated apps — with the feed URL compiled into the signed host (never app-selected), staged≠activated semantics documented as ▲, errors mapped from KELD-UPDATE-*; `keld migrate` translates electron-builder/forge config into keld.build.ts with a per-field disposition report (fuses/ASAR/custom hooks → explained drops); the arch 04 §7 bridge release is constrained by electron-updater's publisherName Authenticode check + NSIS spawn args on Windows and by Squirrel.Mac's designated-requirement check on macOS, and is only reachable for Windows x64 until KEL-137/KEL-103 land. Six decision atoms below; three prototypes; evidence receipts attached.

decisions.question: Which updater contract does the compat layer clone: Electron-core `autoUpdater` (the F09 census) or the electron-updater v6 surface the corpus actually calls?
decisions.proposed_answer: Both, as two thin Bun facades over ONE host-owned KEL-53 state machine: (a) `@keld/electron`.autoUpdater implements the 10-member Electron-core surface for the per-API scoreboard; (b) `keld migrate` rewrites `electron-updater` imports to a Keld-owned shim exporting the AppUpdater subset draw.io exercises (autoDownload, autoInstallOnAppQuit, downloadUpdate, download-progress, update-available(info.version), update-downloaded, error(err), logger, checkForUpdates():Promise<result|null>, quitAndInstall(isSilent?, isForceRunAfter?)). Provider options ({provider:'github', owner, repo, channel}) are parsed only to cross-check against keld.build.ts and never contacted. Zettlr needs neither (custom got downloader) and scores N/A in this family. Declared as an L3 ecosystem row in the KEL-74 denominator, not as Electron API.

decisions.question: How do KEL-53 states map onto the Electron/electron-updater event sequence, and what does `update-downloaded` + `quitAndInstall` mean when Keld's activation can roll back after a failed 30-second health check?
decisions.proposed_answer: Mapping: checking-for-update = feed fetch begins; update-available(info{version, releaseDate=publishedAt, releaseName=version, releaseNotes undefined}) = SelectedFull minted after signature+shape+floor filter; update-not-available = typed empty filtered set; download-progress(percent, transferred, total=full.size, bytesPerSecond) = streamed verify_full bytes (electron-updater shim only); update-downloaded = CompletedWindowsStage exists (staged, verified, NOT published/selected); error(Error{message: KELD-UPDATE-* Display, code}) = any typed refusal, delivered exactly once; quitAndInstall = emit before-quit-for-update → close all windows → before-quit → will-quit → quit → host runs the journaled activation. Documented divergence ▲: 'downloaded' ≠ 'will run next launch'; if the candidate fails health the host rolls back to last-known-good and the next launch runs the OLD version (observable via app.getVersion()). autoInstallOnAppQuit=true (electron-updater default; draw.io's silent path) maps to the same deferred activation at quit. Electron-core autoUpdater's implicit auto-download after update-available is honored; the shim honors autoDownload=false by not fetching the full artifact.

[fact] keld-update windows_extraction: completed stage 'is neither published nor selected and active records/journal stay unchanged' (product-status row 9)

decisions.alternatives_rejected: Emitting update-downloaded only after activation commit: impossible without quitting (activation requires candidate launch), so draw.io's 'Install / Later' dialog would never appear. Emitting error on rollback into the OLD app instance: the old instance was not the caller; instead surface a typed startup diagnostic (KELD-UPDATE-016) and an `error` on the next checkForUpdates. Synchronous throws from facade methods: rejected — electron-updater's throw+event fan-out is the bug draw.io works around; Keld delivers one `error` emission and a rejected promise, never a sync throw.
decisions.unknowns: Whether KEL-53 admits a 'quit without relaunch' activation (electron-updater isForceRunAfter=false / autoInstallOnAppQuit silent install): the transaction needs the candidate to boot and report Ready, so a user-visible relaunch or a headless health boot must be chosen by the KEL-53 owner. Whether electron-updater's checkForUpdates both rejects and emits `error` for the same failure (needs source receipt at the pinned tag) to decide the shim's exactly-once contract.

decisions.question: Where does the facade's authority live and what kipc/guard shape carries it, given Bun roles have zero ambient OS authority and KEL-53 forbids role-writable update state?
decisions.proposed_answer: All network, verification, staging, activation and relaunch stay in the Rust host (keld-update + host lifecycle owner). The main Bun role gets three guarded calls — `update.check` (rate-limited; returns typed result), `update.download` (shim only; honors autoDownload=false), `update.quitAndInstall({silent, forceRunAfter})` — plus a host→Bun event stream (checking/available/not-available/progress/downloaded/error) carrying versions, dates and sizes but never filesystem paths (electron-updater's `downloadedFile`/`updateFile` are undefined ▲). Grants are declared in keld.permissions.jsonc and generated through the existing KEL-98 echo-codegen contract source (no new IDL). Quit sequencing reuses @keld/api app.quit and the F01 before-quit ordering; error text reuses KELD-UPDATE-* Display verbatim.

decisions.question: What must the arch 04 §7 bridge release (final Electron release whose electron-updater feed points at a Keld installer) satisfy on each platform, and in what order can it ship?
decisions.proposed_answer: The bridge is constrained by the CLIENT already in users' hands (electron-updater v6 via GitHub Releases): (Windows NSIS) latest.yml/latest-arm64.yml files[] must list a Keld installer with sha512+size; NsisUpdater verifies the downloaded .exe's Authenticode publisherName against the configured list ('JGraph Ltd'/'draw.io Ltd') — so the Keld installer must be signed by the same publisher; it is then spawned with `--updated`, `/S` (silent), optionally `--force-run`, `/D=<dir>`, via elevate.exe when perMachine — Keld's NSIS installer must tolerate those args. draw.io's Electron install is perMachine; Keld's default is PerUserDirect → the bridge must either ship MachineUacDirect (T4d, not implemented) or uninstall the old machine install, else two installs coexist. (macOS) latest-mac.yml must list a zip; MacUpdater proxies it to Squirrel.Mac, which validates the new bundle against the running app's designated requirement (SecCodeCopyDesignatedRequirement → SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors) → the Keld .app must satisfy the Electron app's DR (same team + bundle id [inference]) and be notarized; blocked on KEL-137 + KEL-103. (Linux) electron-updater only self-updates AppImage; deb/rpm/snap users are ManagedOwner → bridge = AppImage + distro-channel republish; blocked on KEL-137. (MSI/APPX/snap) no electron-updater path → repo-level announcement only. Order: Windows x64 NSIS first (matches KEL-53's first admitted cell), macOS/Linux after KEL-137/KEL-103. The feed must serve both artifact families for the transition window: GitHub Release assets can hold latest*.yml alongside Keld's <channel>/<target>/updates.json(.sig) static tree.

decisions.question: What does `keld migrate` translate from electron-builder JSON/YAML and electron-forge JS configs into keld.build.ts, and how are fuses, ASAR, notarize and signing hooks disposed?
decisions.proposed_answer: Generate keld.build.ts (schema owned by KEL-15/KEL-19 — currently absent) with a per-field disposition report: appId/appBundleId → identity.appId (must equal ExpectedAppIdentity app id); productName/copyright/fileAssociations/extendInfo/UTIs → bundle metadata; files/asar/asar.unpack/extraResource(s) → bundle include/exclude (Keld ships a canonical plain tree; `asar` is dropped with explanation, `original-fs`/app.asar.unpacked paths flagged ✘); win.target nsis/msi → targets; appx/snap/flatpak → ManagedOwner targets with 'no direct updater' note; nsis.perMachine → installMode MachineUacDirect (not yet live) vs default PerUserDirect; publish{provider,channel} → update.feed base + channel∈{stable,beta,canary} (draw.io's `latest-arm64` per-arch channel dissolves into Keld's per-target feed path); mac.hardenedRuntime/entitlements/osxSign/osxNotarize/azureSignOptions/signtoolOptions.publisherName → signing.{mac,win} driven natively by keld build (rcodesign/signtool); custom JS hooks (afterPack fuses.mjs, afterSign notarize.mjs with Quick Look appex embedding, sign-trusted.mjs, forge generateAssets/postMake, Pandoc download) → ✘ 'manual: keld build does not execute arbitrary build hooks'; @electron/fuses → a fuse-disposition table mapping each FuseV1Option to the Keld invariant that subsumes it (RunAsNode/NodeOptions/NodeCliInspect → no inherited env/argv for Bun roles (KEL-75); OnlyLoadAppFromAsar + EmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation → signed full-package contentBlake3 + bound launch path (KEL-53/KEL-254); CookieEncryption → engine profile policy (KEL-135, unknown parity); GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges → webview origin policy (KEL-79)). Forge configs are executable JS: migrate evaluates them in a sandboxed Bun subprocess or asks for `--config-json`; electron-builder JSON/YAML parse statically.
evidence: [fact] arch 04 §2: keld.build.ts 'packaging: targets, signing, update feed, delta settings — generated by migrate (from electron-builder config)'; §2 'Nothing else. No src-tauri/, no Rust files, no new IDL'

[fact] draw.io: 5 electron-builder JSON configs (win nsis+msi perMachine, win-arm64 channel latest-arm64, appx, linux-mac zip/dmg/AppImage/deb/rpm with afterSign notarize.mjs + afterPack fuses.mjs, snap core24); build/fuses.mjs flips RunAsNode=false, CookieEncryption=true, NodeOptions=false, NodeCliInspect=false, OnlyLoadAppFromAsar=true, EmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation=false, LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot=false; notarize.mjs embeds and re-signs a Quick Look .appex then notarytool

[fact] Zettlr: forge.config.js (JS with hooks downloading Pandoc, FusesPlugin in production, osxSign/osxNotarize, asar.unpack '*.{node,dll}', makers deb/rpm/zip) plus electron-builder.yml (dmg, nsis perMachine:false, AppImage, azureSignOptions) used with --prepackaged

[fact] fuses.md: fuses are 'magic bits' flipped before signing; defaults runAsNode on, cookieEncryption off, nodeOptions on, nodeCliInspect on, embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation off, onlyLoadAppFromAsar off, grantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges on; asar-integrity.md: on mismatch 'the app will forcefully terminate'; research 186 rows 8–9: fuses are build hardening not a capability system; ASAR-only lookup and integrity are separate controls
[fact] asar-archives.md: archives read-only; no cwd inside asar; execFile/fs.open/dlopen unpack to temp; original-fs bypass
[fact] arch 06 §3: signing via rcodesign/signtool/osslsigncode, config in keld.build.ts; keld-cli migrate/build reserved KELD-CLI-045; keld.build.ts has no schema in repo (grep)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Executing electron-builder/forge hooks from keld build for parity: runs arbitrary project JS at build time inside Keld's trusted packaging step and re-creates the plugin surface Keld refuses (no custom native, no fifth unique). Emulating ASAR as a virtual filesystem for compat: would need an fs shim in every role and defeats the signed canonical tree; the corpus does not depend on asar paths at runtime beyond Zettlr's native-module unpack (routed to KEL-215 addon workers).
decisions.unknowns: KEL-15 keld.build.ts schema status/owner approval; whether `keld build` will support embedding app extensions (Quick Look .appex) and extra resources (Pandoc binary) — Zettlr/draw.io both need extraResource at minimum; forge-config evaluation policy for migrate.

never_list.surface: autoUpdater.setFeedURL / electron-updater provider options / requestHeaders / headers / serverType / login as feed authority
never_list.rationale: App-selected feed URLs into a privileged updater are on the program never-list; Keld's key/app id/channel/target are compiled into the signed host (arch 06 §4a step 1; research 186 row 10).
KEL-53's monotonic protected floor is the replay/downgrade defense; honoring downgrade flags would reopen it.

never_list.surface: App-executed installers or exposure of staged artifact paths (electron-updater downloadedFile/updateFile, NsisUpdater spawn, Zettlr shell.openPath of an installer)
never_list.rationale: KEL-53 forbids arbitrary relaunch helpers and role-writable update state; raw spawn from strict roles is never-listed.
Candidate launch is host-owned under the exact initiating token; app-chosen exec paths are a privilege path.

never_list.surface: Electron's MSIX self-update path and any direct mutation of store/package-manager installs
never_list.rationale: ManagedOwner mode refuses direct activation and registers no competing writer (arch 06, KEL-53 non-goals).

never_list.surface: @electron/fuses as a runtime or permission API
never_list.rationale: Fuses are Electron-binary hardening bits; Keld's equivalents are host invariants, not app-toggled flags (research 186 row 8).

never_list.surface: ASAR virtual filesystem / original-fs / app.asar.unpacked path contracts
never_list.rationale: Keld ships a signed canonical plain tree; an fs shim per role would duplicate FsBroker policy.

never_list.surface: Executing electron-builder/forge JS hooks (afterPack/afterSign/custom sign scripts) inside keld build
never_list.rationale: Arbitrary project code inside the trusted packaging/signing step and a plugin surface Keld does not offer; declarative signing config only.

never_list.surface: Running Electron's api-autoupdater-*-spec.ts under Bun as the oracle
never_list.rationale: Research 214 refuses running Electron's spec tree; cite test identities via an approved per-surface spec and land Keld-owned tests.
